title: Aluminum Works
shortDescription: Premium aluminum facades, doors & windows with the latest designs
description: We specialize in designing, installing, and finishing all aluminum works for residential, commercial, and industrial buildings. We use the finest globally certified aluminum with a wide range of finishes and colors to suit every project.
benefits: High resistance to rust and corrosion

process.title: Requirements Study
process.description: We analyze your project needs and understand your architectural vision

process.title: Engineering Design
process.description: We prepare execution drawings and engineering plans

process.title: Manufacturing
process.description: Precision manufacturing of components in our equipped workshop

process.title: Installation & Handover
process.description: Professional installation with quality and safety assurance

faq.question: How long does an aluminum project take?
faq.answer: Execution time ranges from 2 to 8 weeks depending on project size and complexity. Small-scale work like doors and windows typically takes 1–2 weeks, while full tower facades can extend to 16 weeks including coordination with the main contractor.

faq.question: Do you offer warranties on aluminum works?
faq.answer: Yes, we offer a comprehensive 5-year warranty covering both materials and workmanship, including any manufacturing defects. We also offer optional annual preventive maintenance contracts after the warranty period expires.

faq.question: What types of aluminum do you use?
faq.answer: We use 6063-T5 and 6061-T6 alloy sections from certified European and Turkish suppliers. All aluminum materials are tested per EN 755 and ASTM B221 standards and carry SASO Saudi conformity certificates.

faq.question: Does aluminum hold up to the heat and humidity in Saudi Arabia?
faq.answer: Aluminum is one of the most suitable materials for the Saudi climate. The electrostatic powder coating or anodizing finish we apply protects sections from corrosion caused by extreme heat, sand, and coastal humidity — maintaining appearance for decades without fading or peeling.

faq.question: Do you comply with Saudi Building Code (SBC)?
faq.answer: Compliance with SBC and SBC-601 Energy Code is mandatory in all our projects. We provide thermal insulation calculation extracts and facade performance verification per national requirements, facilitating building permit approvals and final inspections.

faq.question: Can colors and finishes be customized?
faq.answer: Absolutely. We offer over 200 standard RAL colors plus custom finishes including wood-grain effect, metallic textures, matte and gloss solids. We provide physical samples for approval before production begins — no surprises at handover.

faq.question: How do you handle renovation and replacement projects?
faq.answer: We have a dedicated refurbishment team. We measure existing openings and manufacture matching profiles without touching the structural frame, minimizing operational downtime. This covers window replacement in existing towers, mall entrances, and residential villas.

faq.question: Do you provide 3D visualization before execution?
faq.answer: Yes, we use AutoCAD, Revit, and Rhinoceros to deliver full 3D facade simulations before manufacturing starts. This lets you review the final appearance, approve colors and details, and make any changes — with zero surprises at handover.

faq.question: Is there a minimum project size you accept?
faq.answer: We welcome all project sizes, from replacing a single window in a residential villa to full multi-storey tower facades. For smaller projects we offer a rapid supply-and-install service; for larger ones we assign a dedicated project team including a project manager, site engineer, and specialist supervisors.

faq.question: How is aluminum work priced?
faq.answer: Pricing is based on several factors: aluminum weight used (linear meters), finish type and complexity, accompanying insulation and glass specifications, and labor and installation costs. We issue a detailed line-item quote within 48 hours of receiving drawings and specifications — with every element listed separately for easy comparison.

faq.question: Do you work as a subcontractor for other contractors or developers?
faq.answer: Yes, we serve main contractors and other construction companies as a nominated specialist subcontractor. We have extensive experience operating within multi-contractor projects and adhering to payment schedule requirements and quality standards for large-scale and government projects.

faq.question: Can you supply aluminum sections without installation?
faq.answer: Yes. We offer a supply-only service for contractors and fabricators who have their own installation crews. All sections are cut to length, labelled, and packaged per shop drawings, with a full material certificate and packing list included for site receiving inspection.

faq.question: How do you handle site measurements for irregular openings?
faq.answer: Our site survey team uses laser distance meters and digital level tools to capture all opening dimensions to ±1 mm. We then produce a site measurement report that is cross-checked against architectural drawings before any cutting order is placed, eliminating fit-up errors on site.

faq.question: Do you provide shop drawings and as-built drawings?
faq.answer: Yes. We issue full shop drawings for client and consultant approval before fabrication, and as-built drawings upon project completion. Both sets are delivered in DWG and PDF formats and are archived in our document management system for the lifetime of the warranty.

faq.question: What acoustic performance can aluminum window systems achieve?
faq.answer: Our thermally broken double-glazed aluminum window systems achieve Rw values of 35–45 dB depending on glass specification and profile depth. For high-noise environments such as airports or urban motorways, we can specify specialist acoustic interlayer glass and heavy-duty sealing gaskets to push performance beyond 45 dB.

faq.question: Are your aluminum systems tested for water and air infiltration?
faq.answer: Yes. All curtain wall and window systems we supply are type-tested to AAMA 501, ASTM E283 (air infiltration) and ASTM E331 (water resistance) by accredited laboratories. Test reports are available for review and are submitted as part of the project submittal package to the engineer of record.

faq.question: Can you match existing aluminum profiles on a heritage or partially renovated building?
faq.answer: In most cases, yes. We maintain a library of legacy extrusion profiles and can commission custom die extrusions for profiles no longer in standard production. We also carry a wide stock of universal bridging profiles that allow new sections to connect seamlessly to original frames.

title: Glass Works
shortDescription: Comprehensive glass solutions for facades, partitions & entrances
description: We provide comprehensive glass solutions including full glass facades, interior glass partitions, and transparent roofing. We use the latest tempered and double-glazed glass technologies to ensure the highest safety and insulation standards.

process.title: Engineering Consultation
process.description: Assess requirements and select the appropriate glass type

process.title: Design & Measurement
process.description: Precise measurements and preparation of execution drawings

process.title: Manufacturing & Cutting
process.description: Glass manufacturing and cutting with millimeter precision

process.title: Professional Installation
process.description: Safe installation with quality tests and sealing

faq.question: What types of glass are available?
faq.answer: We offer a wide range including: Insulated Glass Units (IGU) with air or argon fill for enhanced thermal performance, heat-tempered safety glass, laminated glass, heat-strengthened glass, Low-E coated glass, smart switchable glass (PDLC/SPD), and ultra-clear low-iron glass for maximum transparency.

faq.question: How do you ensure installation safety?
faq.answer: We follow an integrated safety protocol: certified structural silicone from Dow Corning and Sika, air-pressure and water-penetration tests per ASTM E283 and E331, and supervision by a licensed structural engineer at every installation stage — with a quality report delivered to the client.

faq.question: Is glass safe in the hot climate and under intense sunlight in Saudi Arabia?
faq.answer: Yes, particularly with the right product selection. We recommend Low-E glass with a vapor-deposited coating for high-solar-radiation zones. This reduces the Solar Heat Gain Coefficient (SHGC) to 0.25 or below, cutting air-conditioning loads by up to 40% compared to standard clear glass.

faq.question: What glass thickness is appropriate for high-rise buildings?
faq.answer: Thickness is determined by wind-load calculations per ASCE 7 and SBC-301. For commercial towers we typically supply double units in the 28–36 mm total range (e.g. 6+12+6 or 8+12+8 mm), with a signed structural calculation report issued for each project.

faq.question: What warranty do you offer on glass and fittings?
faq.answer: We provide: a 10-year warranty against thermal seal failure (internal condensation) on IGU units, a 5-year warranty on sealants and weatherproofing materials, and a 2-year workmanship warranty on installation labor. Any unit showing manufacturing defects within the warranty period is replaced at no cost.

faq.question: Can you handle curved glass and non-standard shapes?
faq.answer: Yes, we work with architecturally complex forms including cylindrically curved glass, angled panels, and custom geometric patterns. We rely on made-to-measure manufacturing and partner with specialized European factories for shapes that exceed local processing capabilities.

faq.question: How are glass facades cleaned and maintained?
faq.answer: We supply a detailed maintenance manual with every project. Generally, external cleaning every 3–6 months is recommended (more frequent in sandy regions) using non-acidic solutions. We also provide a unit-registry log with data for each glass panel, making future replacement straightforward.

faq.question: Do you handle fire-rated glass requirements?
faq.answer: Yes, we supply fire-rated glass with EW and EI classifications per EN 1364 and Saudi Civil Defense requirements. This is used in fire-compartment partitions, escape-route doors, and interior divisions in facilities with strict safety mandates such as hospitals, hotels, and government buildings.

faq.question: Can you install acoustic glass for offices and hospitals?
faq.answer: Yes. We supply double and triple IGU units with argon fill and an asymmetric cavity (e.g. 6+12+8 mm) to break the sound resonance frequency and achieve an STC rating of 38–45 dB. Ideal for offices adjacent to highways, boardrooms, and healthcare facilities requiring high speech-privacy standards.

faq.question: How do you handle leaks or breakage after project handover?
faq.answer: We provide an after-sales hotline during business hours. For warranty-covered leaks or breakages, we dispatch an emergency team within 24–48 hours to assess the situation and provide a temporary fix while the permanent repair is arranged. Every project has a digital panel registry that speeds up sourcing replacement units.

faq.question: Can glass be printed or patterned for privacy and branding?
faq.answer: Yes. We supply digitally printed ceramic-frit glass for logos, geometric patterns, and gradient privacy screens. The ink is kiln-fired into the glass surface at 650 °C, making it fully permanent and UV-resistant. We also offer sandblasted and acid-etched finishes for a frosted aesthetic without printing.

faq.question: What is the lead time for ordering specialty glass?
faq.answer: Standard tempered and double-glazed units are produced in 2–4 weeks. Specialty products such as Low-E coated, laminated, printed, or curved glass typically require 4–8 weeks depending on origin. We always communicate lead times upfront and factor them into the project master schedule.

faq.question: Do you offer structural glazing (bonded glass without visible frames)?
faq.answer: Yes. We design and install structural silicone-bonded (SSG) facades where the glass is bonded to aluminum mullions with two-part Dow Corning or Sika structural sealant, creating a flush, frameless appearance. SSG systems are tested and approved by the sealant manufacturer's technical team on every project.

faq.question: Can glass partitions be reconfigured after installation?
faq.answer: Demountable aluminum-framed glass partition systems are specifically designed for future reconfiguration. We offer both full-height and ceiling-track systems with modular panel widths, allowing offices to be subdivided or opened up without creating construction waste or requiring significant structural changes.

faq.question: How do you manage glass transportation and on-site storage safely?
faq.answer: All glass is transported in custom-built A-frame stillages with foam spacers and polycarbonate corner protectors. On site, glass is stored upright on rubber-padded racks away from traffic routes. Our logistics team provides a delivery schedule synchronized with the installation programme to minimize breakage risk from prolonged site storage.

faq.question: Are there glass options that reduce solar glare without heavy tinting?
faq.answer: Yes. Selective-coated Low-E glass achieves a Light-to-Solar-Gain (LSG) ratio above 2.0, meaning it admits twice as much visible light as solar heat. This eliminates the dark-tinted appearance of traditional reflective glass while still meeting ASHRAE 90.1 and SBC-601 energy performance requirements.

title: Steel Works
shortDescription: Durable steel structures for large industrial and commercial projects
description: We specialize in designing, manufacturing, and installing steel structures for industrial, commercial, and infrastructure projects. Our specialized team ensures the highest standards of engineering precision and durability.
benefits: High durability and long service life
Resistant to earthquakes and heavy loads
applications: Steel structures for factories and warehouses

process.title: Design & Detailing
process.description: Detailed execution drawings for every structural element

process.title: Installation & Inspection
process.description: Scheduled installation with quality and safety inspections

faq.question: Do you offer periodic maintenance for steel structures?
faq.answer: Yes, we offer tiered maintenance programs: an annual visual inspection, a non-destructive testing (NDT) inspection every 3 years, and a full coating and anti-corrosion renewal every 5–7 years. Each inspection is documented in a detailed report filed in the project record.

faq.question: What is the typical execution time for a steel structure project?
faq.answer: Execution ranges from 4 to 16 weeks. Small-scale projects like canopies and barriers take 4–6 weeks; large manufacturing warehouses or tower structures may take 12–20 weeks. We provide a detailed Gantt Chart timeline at project kick-off.

faq.question: What quality standards do you follow in fabrication?
faq.answer: We comply with AISC (American Institute of Steel Construction), AWS D1.1 for structural welding, and Saudi Building Code SBC-301. All steel materials carry ASTM A36/A572 certification and undergo tensile and hardness testing before fabrication begins.

faq.question: How do you protect steel structures from rust in coastal areas?
faq.answer: We apply a multi-layer protection system: Sa2.5 abrasive blast cleaning, a zinc-rich primer at 75 microns, an epoxy intermediate coat at 125 microns, and a polyurethane or polysiloxane topcoat at 75 microns. For severe coastal environments, COR-TEN weathering steel is also available.

faq.question: Are steel structures safe from earthquakes in Saudi Arabia?
faq.answer: Steel is one of the most earthquake-resistant materials due to its ductility and energy-dissipation capacity. We design all structures per SBC-301 Chapter 12 seismic requirements, accounting for region-specific hazard maps across Saudi Arabia.

faq.question: Can steel structures be combined with glass facades and aluminum?
faq.answer: This is one of our key competitive advantages. Since we specialize in all three trades — steel, glass, and aluminum — under one roof, we deliver integrated solutions that include the load-bearing steel frame, the glass facade system, and the aluminum profiles in a single contract, eliminating scope conflicts and reducing overall cost.

faq.question: What is the difference between structural steel and cold-formed sections for decorative work?
faq.answer: Structural steel (H, I, RHS sections) is used for load-bearing elements like bridges, columns, and beams. Cold-formed sections (tubes, angles, and light profiles) are used for staircases, balustrades, and decorative canopies. We supply both to the correct specification for each application.

faq.question: Can an existing steel structure be modified or expanded?
faq.answer: Yes — flexibility is one of steel's greatest advantages. We conduct a structural assessment of the existing facility first to determine its load capacity, then design expansion or modification elements that integrate with the original frame. Expansions are often completed without fully halting factory or warehouse operations.

faq.question: Do you offer custom fabrication for non-standard parts?
faq.answer: Yes. Our workshop is equipped with CNC laser cutters and bending machines capable of fabricating any steel element per execution drawings to a tolerance of ±1 mm. We serve architects and designers who need unique pieces for decorative or structural applications that fall outside standard rolled-section sizes.

faq.question: What is your monthly production capacity?
faq.answer: Our current in-house production capacity is approximately 800 tonnes of fabricated steel per month, with the ability to scale through our certified manufacturing partners for projects exceeding that volume. We share a production-capacity schedule with the client at contract signing to guarantee alignment with the project timeline.

faq.question: Do you provide structural calculations signed by a licensed Saudi engineer?
faq.answer: Yes. All structural calculations are reviewed and stamped by engineers registered with the Saudi Council of Engineers (SCE). These reports provide the official documentation required for building-permit issuance and government handover procedures.

faq.question: What welding certifications do your welders hold?
faq.answer: All structural welders are qualified to AWS D1.1 and hold valid Welding Procedure Specifications (WPS). Welder qualification records (WQR) are maintained on file and are available for client or third-party inspector review. For critical joints we apply 100% visual inspection plus UT or MT non-destructive testing.

faq.question: Can steel structures be hot-dip galvanized instead of painted?
faq.answer: Yes. For outdoor structures, buried elements, or high-humidity environments, hot-dip galvanizing to ISO 1461 provides superior long-term protection with a zinc layer of 85–100 microns. Galvanized structures typically require no maintenance for 20–40 years depending on environment, compared to 5–7 years for a paint system.

faq.question: Do you supply steel mezzanine floors for warehouses?
faq.answer: Yes. We design and install freestanding mezzanine decks with structural steel columns, primary and secondary beams, and either steel grating, checker-plate, or oriented-strand-board decking. We provide full load calculations and PE-stamped drawings, and mezzanines can be designed for easy disassembly and relocation.

faq.question: How do you handle interference between structural steel and MEP services?
faq.answer: We coordinate structural steel with mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) drawings using BIM clash-detection software (Navisworks or Revit) before fabrication. Web penetrations for ducts and conduits are designed with reinforced openings, and all coordination drawings are shared with the MEP subcontractors for approval.

faq.question: What is your approach to on-site safety during steel erection?
faq.answer: We comply with Saudi Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) regulations and OSHA Steel Erection Standard 29 CFR 1926 Subpart R. Every erection crew uses full-body harnesses, inertia reels, and designated anchor points. A site-specific erection method statement and lifting plan are approved by the project safety officer before work begins.
